title: Victoria Park Master Plan recommended for approval
subtitle: Chandler Mowat Community Centre funding, election compliance committee, noise exemptions and a development charges complaint adjournment.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended approval of the Victoria Park Master Plan {{vote:m5}}. The plan sets out near-term and long-term work for the park, subject to annual budget approvals. Staff said about half of the implementation funding comes from development charges, so some projects could be scaled back when the 2027 budget is set.

The committee also recommended reallocating existing capital funding from closed-out projects to pay for interior renovations at the Chandler Mowat Community Centre {{vote:m6}}. It recommended setting up a joint Municipal Elections Compliance Audit Committee for the 2026-2030 term {{vote:m1}}, and adjourning a development charges complaint about 15 Dellroy Avenue until no later than August 10, 2026 {{vote:m4}}.

Two noise exemptions were also recommended: one for the Holy Trinity Serbian Orthodox Church's September BBQ and Bull Roast {{vote:m2}}, and one for summer events at Bingemans, with conditions {{vote:m3}}. These recommendations go to Council for a final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the master plan and direct staff to carry out its near- and long-term recommendations, subject to annual budget approvals.
The committee recommended that Council reallocate existing capital funding from completed or closed-out projects to help fund interior renovations at the centre.

The committee recommended establishing a joint compliance audit committee for the 2026-2030 term and delegating to the City Clerk the authority to revise its terms of reference and to select, appoint and compensate its members.
The committee recommended adjourning the complaint until no later than August 10, 2026.
The committee recommended a noise exemption for events at 425 Bingeman Centre Drive, conditional on responding to staff requests and keeping an on-site contact available.

decisions.item: Holy Trinity Serbian Church noise exemption
decisions.detail: The committee recommended a noise exemption for the church's annual BBQ and Bull Roast on September 5 and 6, 2026.

debate: Several councillors said the park is a citywide destination and supported investing in it. Some also asked that parks in general get more attention in upcoming budgets, including parks outside the downtown.

Funding was the main concern. Staff said about half of the implementation budget is funded by development charges, and one councillor cautioned that the capital forecast will need close review because of provincial changes. Staff confirmed final approval of the implementation would return through the budget process.

One councillor asked why the playground surface was prioritized over the splash pad. Staff said the rubberized surfacing is at the end of its life, and that engagement results and criteria put it first. The councillor asked that the splash pad be moved up if budget allows.

Questions on safety and access covered lighting gaps near the Iron Horse Trail crossing, a possible mid-block crossing on Jubilee, and an electrical outlet for food truck vendors to address noise and fumes. Staff said these are addressed in the plan.

On Chandler Mowat, staff said using closeout funds is the appropriate way to seek approval for extra funding, and that no other projects are queued for the centre. One councillor said they dislike mid-term funding changes like this but supported it because of the need.
